  "title": "10/23 Mkt Internal Wkly: Trend vs Volatility: Long-Duration Capital vs. Short-Duration Rebalancing",
  "type": "sales_trading",

  "insights": [
   "Rebecca Cheong (UBS Sales and Trading, not UBS Research) keeps a medium-term bullish view on U.S. equities despite the recent Hedge Fund and Systematic unwinds.",
   "The main structural change in U.S. equity markets over 15 years is the growing weight of long-duration capital (Retail Investors, Retirement Assets, Foreign Investors) next to fast growth in short-duration trading capital (Systematic, Quantitative, Hedge Fund strategies).",
   "Long-duration capital increasingly drives market trends and short-duration capital increasingly drives volatility. Corrections have become more frequent and sharper, and recoveries faster and more persistent.",
   "Short-term volatility and long-term direction are treated as separate forces. Unless the drivers of capital persistence deteriorate meaningfully, systematic deleveraging is more likely to create temporary dislocations than durable changes to the long-term trend.",
   "Hedge Funds and Systematic Strategies are a relatively small share of aggregate ownership. They have limited influence on long-term direction, but their high turnover, leverage and model-driven trading drive short-term volatility.",
   "Traditional Pension ownership has declined and has gradually been replaced by Retail-Directed Retirement Assets, which raises structural equity allocations as retirement assets move into more equity-oriented vehicles.",
   "Implications cited: extended and accelerated rallies driven by leverage, product innovation and structural inflows, more frequent V-shaped recoveries, and more persistent buy-the-dip behavior from Retail and Foreign Investors supported by recurring retirement contributions."
  ],
